boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase outings around Loras College, including city parks, trails, public art, river views, and free library activities.

cards.title: Picnic Above Downtown
cards.subtitle: Allison-Henderson Park, beside Loras College
cards.notes: Bring snacks from home, claim a picnic table, and compare downtown views from this city park at 1500 Loras Boulevard.
cards.short_summary: A free picnic and skyline-view meetup directly beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Allison-Henderson Park at 1500 Loras Boulevard, and its published admission policy states that admission to city parks is free except for motor vehicles entering Eagle Point Park.
cards.access_notes: City parks are open year-round; seasonal amenities generally operate from the first Saturday in May through the fourth Sunday in October.

cards.title: Circle the Gazebo and Time Capsule
cards.subtitle: Washington Park in downtown Dubuque
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths, examine the gazebo, and find the city time capsule scheduled to be opened in 2076.
cards.short_summary: A downtown garden stroll centered on two distinctive landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The official park page identifies Washington Park's plants, gazebo, seating, picnic tables, fountains, and time capsule; city policy states park admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Regular listed hours are 7 a.m.–10 p.m. from the first Saturday in May through the fourth Sunday in October; no reservation is needed for an ordinary walk.

cards.title: Shoot Hoops at Comiskey
cards.subtitle: Comiskey Park outdoor basketball courts
cards.notes: Bring a basketball for a casual shootaround, then cool down beneath the shaded picnic shelters without reserving one.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor basketball meetup with nearby shaded seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Comiskey Park page lists outdoor basketball courts, shaded picnic shelters, a skate park, tennis court, field, playground, and splash pad; city parks have free admission.
cards.access_notes: The park lists daily hours of 8 a.m.–10 p.m. from the first Saturday in May through the fourth Sunday in October; bring your own ball.

cards.title: Walk the Bee Branch Loop
cards.subtitle: Bee Branch Creek Greenway trail system
cards.notes: Choose the marked 0.82-mile upper or lower loop and walk beside the restored creek with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A measured urban trail loop suited to an easy social walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City documents two measured 0.82-mile loops at Bee Branch Creek Greenway and states that the trail system connects to Dubuque's riverfront and Mines of Spain trails.
cards.access_notes: Use the public trail during posted park hours. Walking requires no ticket or purchase; check the city trail map for the preferred loop.

cards.title: Follow the Mississippi Riverwalk
cards.subtitle: Port of Dubuque riverfront trail
cards.notes: Start near East Third Street and walk the riverfront together, pausing at public overlooks and outdoor artworks.
cards.short_summary: A purchase-free riverfront walk through the Port of Dubuque.
cards.evidence_claim: The City's current recreational-trails page includes the Mississippi Riverwalk within its 43-mile public bike-and-hike trail system of paved routes for walking, hiking, and biking.
cards.access_notes: This is a public recreational trail with no admission or required purchase. Follow posted signs and yield appropriately to cyclists.

cards.entity_name: Trolley Line Trail at Eagle Point Park
cards.title: Walk the Old Trolley Route
cards.subtitle: Pedestrian entry to Eagle Point Park
cards.notes: Enter on foot and follow the half-mile paved former streetcar route, stopping at its midpoint artwork.
cards.short_summary: A free pedestrian route combining park history, artwork, and river scenery.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that pedestrians and bicyclists enter Eagle Point Park free; its Trolley Line Trail is a half-mile paved bike-and-hike route following the former streetcar line.
cards.access_notes: Enter as a pedestrian or bicyclist for free. Motor vehicles cost $1 and buses $5; regular in-season hours begin at 7 a.m.

cards.title: Compare River Views from Murphy Park
cards.subtitle: Louis Murphy Park overlook
cards.notes: Walk to the overlook, identify landmarks across southern Dubuque, and use an unreserved picnic table for conversation.
cards.short_summary: A hilltop gathering with broad views over the city and Mississippi River.
cards.evidence_claim: The official page identifies Louis Murphy Park as an 80-acre public park overlooking southern Dubuque and the Mississippi River; the City's admission policy makes ordinary park entry free.
cards.access_notes: Ordinary park access requires no admission or purchase. Use open picnic areas rather than any pavilion reserved for a private group.

cards.title: Walk the Memorial Boardwalk
cards.subtitle: Veterans Memorial Plaza at McAleece Park
cards.notes: Follow the swirling path onto the pond boardwalk, then view the Skyward sculpture and granite globe.
cards.short_summary: A reflective public-art walk through Dubuque's veterans memorial complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The City documents the plaza's granite globe and a decorative path leading to an elevated pond boardwalk and the Skyward sculpture; admission to city parks is free.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is a public city-park feature with no admission or required purchase. Treat memorial elements respectfully and remain on designated paths.

cards.title: Meet at the Inclusive Playground
cards.subtitle: Veterans Memorial Park and Miracle League
cards.notes: Gather at the all-inclusive playground for accessible outdoor recreation designed for children and adults of varied abilities.
cards.short_summary: An accessible, no-admission recreation stop for an all-ages group.
cards.evidence_claim: The City's facility page says the Miracle League complex at Veterans Memorial Park offers an all-inclusive playground and baseball field for children and adults of all abilities.
cards.access_notes: The complex is open daily from 7 a.m.–10 p.m. Ordinary playground access requires no admission or purchase; organized field use may be scheduled.

cards.title: Host a Free Wi-Fi Work Session
cards.subtitle: Carnegie-Stout Public Library
cards.notes: Bring charged devices, connect to the public Wi-Fi, and work side by side without buying drinks or obtaining a guest card.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor study meetup with public internet access.
cards.evidence_claim: The library's official FAQ states that free wireless internet is available to the public throughout the building and immediately outside it.
cards.access_notes: Public Wi-Fi needs no purchase. Current listed hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–7 p.m., Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.
